assertions.text: Output contains a markdown table (using | column | syntax)
assertions.evidence: | Scenario | Credit Score | Applicant Age | Income Status | Min Score...

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Eligible?' or 'Approved?')
Column names use domain/business language — no implementation terms like 'creditScore', 'isEligible', 'boolean', 'int'
assertions.evidence: Credit Score, Applicant Age, Income Status, Min Score (Threshold), Approved?, Rejection Reason?

assertions.text: Table includes at least one row specifically for the senior applicant (65+) threshold scenario
assertions.evidence: Senior age boundary — exactly 65 | 620 | 65 | stable | 600 | yes

assertions.text: The missing income scenario is represented — either as a row with an open/uncertain expected value (?, TBD, or blank) or as an explicit open question note
Scenario names describe conditions ('Senior applicant at threshold') not outcomes ('Approved')
assertions.evidence: Standard approval and Senior approval above senior threshold mention outcomes, not just conditions

assertions.text: The policy thresholds (650 for standard, 600 for senior) appear as concrete values in the Credit Score column
assertions.evidence: 650 appears in 3 rows, 600 appears in 3 rows of Credit Score column

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
Policy thresholds (650/600 credit scores) appear in a dedicated policy column separate from the applicant's actual credit score column
assertions.evidence: Min Score (Threshold) column shows 650 and 600 values separate from Credit Score column

assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms (e.g. '65', '700', 'Stable', 'yes', 'no') — not abstract codes or raw booleans
assertions.evidence: stable, unstable, yes, no, 700, 650, 65, 40 used throughout

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules
assertions.evidence: Single table mixes age boundaries, credit thresholds, and income status concerns

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns
assertions.evidence: Single 15-row table combines all concerns, creating permutations like age+credit+income

assertions.text: Age boundary policy, credit score categorisation, and income status are separated into distinct tables, with a final table combining these for the expected verdict
assertions.evidence: All three concerns appear in one table; no separate tables for age, credit, or income
